tldr: Fuse cannot easily take returns and goods-in ASNs (same DESADV message type) in one folder; Fuse segments by landing folder, so changing it would be a substantial rebuild and hurt timelines.
Aim is to go live for March, so the team is looking to solve the routing upstream at SAP or Edicom level instead.
Ingrid will ask Edicom whether returns and kitting/work orders, which come from different IDOCs in SAP, can be routed to separate folders, giving three folders for the same EDI message.
Egress (confirmations) also uses a separate folder, but that is less of a concern; no message content change is needed, only landing location.
Connection: Fuse SFTP offers only public key authentication; AS2 or VAN is not available. Ingrid will take this back to Edicom.
decisions: Do not rebuild Fuse to split returns by content for now; first try to solve the folder routing upstream with Edicom/SAP.
Reconvene if Edicom cannot route returns and kitting to separate folders.

actions.text: Speak with Edicom about routing returns and kitting/work-order messages (separate SAP IDOCs) to separate folders, and report back.
Raise with Edicom the connection issue: Fuse SFTP supports only public key authentication, not user/password, AS2 or VAN.
Check whether work orders (kitting) use the same message type as returns and so also need a separate folder.
Share the Fuse folder structure (create_work_orders, create_purchase_order, create_return_goods_authorization, plus confirmation folders) with Ingrid, as it is in an earlier email.
Schedule a follow-up call if one is needed once Edicom responds.

questions: Can Edicom or SAP route returns and kitting messages into separate folders from goods-in ASNs?
Do work orders (kitting) use the same message type as returns, and so need their own folder?
Can the connection use AS2 or a VAN instead of SFTP, given Edicom's trouble with key-based authentication? Harry said Fuse offers only public key SFTP.
What would a more detailed Fuse-side assessment of splitting by content show, and could it fit the March go-live?
